title: Why a spinning top doesn't fall

scenes.text: Why doesn't a spinning top fall over?
Stand a top up without spin, and gravity tips it over instantly.
But when it spins, every part is whirling in a circle, carrying angular momentum.
Gravity still pulls, but instead of tipping the top, it nudges the spin axis sideways.
So the top slowly circles. That's precession.
Friction steals the spin, the wobble grows, and only then does it fall.
